required_presentation_changes.prior: An aircraft can have a contractual acceptance date, a departure date and an arrival at its receiving unit. The inherited EX16 record establishes a receiving-unit arrival, which should not be relabeled as formal contractual acceptance without the corresponding document. reviewed_section_hashes.heading: Project baselines are not the whole production program
Qualification needs a product and an accepting authority
The next decisive evidence

required_presentation_changes.prior: Budget volumes can provide detailed project and subproject estimates. Those tables are not automatically a complete multi-site capability lifecycle estimate or an integrated program schedule. GAO recommendation status adds an independent oversight question with its own exact recommendation identity. Agency concurrence or a forecast does not establish implementation or closure. Readers should keep the program-baseline question distinct from whether a particular facility or production process has achieved a defined milestone. Neither category can substitute for the other.
required_presentation_changes.replacement: Budget volumes provide project and subproject estimates, not automatically a complete multi-site capability lifecycle estimate or integrated program schedule. The retained September 10 review records GAO-23-104661 recommendation 1 on the cost estimate and GAO-20-703 recommendation 3 on the integrated schedule as Open on the official pages then inspected. Their April 2026 status narratives, agency forecasts and September retrieval date are different dates with different meanings. Agency concurrence or closure of adjacent recommendations does not establish implementation or closure of these exact requirements. Keep program-baseline evidence separate from facility and product milestones; this assessment performs no new GAO-status check.

required_presentation_changes.prior: A first production unit can be an important event without establishing recurring output at a planned rate. A useful production account would identify the product, site, period and status of units produced, qualified, rejected, reworked and accepted. Broad descriptions of enterprise quality or stockpile-management functions do not supply those quantities. The same discipline applies to a construction milestone: accepted facilities and accepted products involve different criteria. The report should explain their relationship without assuming that one demonstrates the other.
required_presentation_changes.replacement: The dated NNSA release, as recorded in the retained September 24 review, was published October 2, 2024 and reports a first qualified unit on October 1. That unit-level milestone is not a September 2026 event, recurring production rate, accepted annual capacity or SRPPF output. Undated overview wording about earlier capability must not override the dated announcement. A recurring production account would still need compatible site, period and produced, qualified, rejected, reworked and accepted-unit definitions. Accepted facilities and accepted products involve different criteria; neither a broad enterprise description nor one milestone supplies the missing series.

required_presentation_changes.prior: The strongest continuation would provide a compatible site-period output return with qualification and acceptance definitions, including revisions and excluded units. A separate accepted-capacity record could clarify infrastructure readiness, while exact GAO closure evidence would answer the program-baseline question. These independent strands should retain their own dates and authority. The September profile incorporates no later recheck and assigns no new stage. It offers readers a precise way to distinguish physical progress, a qualified unit, recurring production and independent oversight, leaving broader capability and cost-performance conclusions to the corresponding evidence.
required_presentation_changes.replacement: This dated assessment incorporates the retained September 10 baseline review and September 24 accepted-capacity review, not a new external recheck. The latter located draft environmental-review material and the earlier unit announcement but not the exact final accepted operating-capacity artifact. Its bounded search does not prove that capability or an acceptance record does not exist. It explicitly does not claim PDF visual or signature verification or inspection of technical production methods. A final accepted-capacity instrument, a compatible recurring qualified-output return and exact GAO recommendation closure remain separate evidence requirements with their own dates and authorities.
